implementation_notes: Go decides interface satisfaction statically, so an interface implementation cannot be created at run time: the proxy is generated as ordinary source code - a struct holding a handler plus one forwarding method per interface method - and checked in, which is how go-gen-proxy, mockgen and gRPC stubs work. When only a function-valued seam needs interception, reflect.MakeFunc builds a typed function value at run time; when nothing needs intercepting, embedding the target interface promotes its whole method set in one line. The reflective proxy of Java or .NET has no Go equivalent, and generation must be wired into the build (go:generate or a CI check) to stay in step with the interface.
pitfalls: Generated proxies drift from their interface unless regeneration runs in CI; go:generate is not enforced by the compiler, so a stale proxy fails late.
reflect.MakeFunc panics when the handler returns the wrong number or type of values, and callers see that panic at call time rather than at generation time.
Embedding forwards the method set but cannot intercept it, and it promotes value-receiver methods while missing pointer-receiver methods when the embedded field is a value.
